title: How Closing One Sea Reprices an Entire Harvest
subtitle: The loss of the Sea of Azov pushed grain onto more expensive land routes, and strikes on Black Sea terminals then closed the alternative.

source.name: Russian grain export logistics and terminal operations reporting

data.label: The Sea of Azov stops working
data.detail: Attacks on shipping rendered the basin non-operational; it carried just over a third of Russian wheat exports.

data.label: The season loses volume
data.detail: Expected decrease in exports for the 2026-2027 season attributed to the closure alone.

data.label: Land haulage takes over
data.detail: Moving grain overland to Black Sea ports adds cost, and that transport is 27.4% dearer than last year.

data.label: The fallback port is hit
data.detail: Ukraine struck the Taman grain terminal on 30 July and its operations stopped.

data.label: Novorossiysk throttles back
data.detail: The two remaining Novorossiysk grain terminals limited exports by the end of the week.

supportingFacts.label: Combined annual capacity of the three affected terminals against total Russian grain exports.
Domestic and export grain prices fell by 8.6% to 12.2% while the cost of reaching a working port increased.

metadata.keyFinding: Closing the Azov basin pushed grain onto costlier routes that were then attacked in turn.
